frozen: 2026-11-24, before any variant was built (with CONTRACT.md; committed before v1..v5 existed)

requirements.name: The left panel decides what every tab shows
requirements.why: Zach, Nov 24: "basically its like a filter side panel on the left, tabs on the top, and then various dashboards like views on each page"; and on the coverage page: "it lets us filter specifically and then see the analysis on all of the views. Its kinda like tensor flow".
requirements.passCondition: A pick in the left panel (dataset, split, speed, config, a regex) re-aggregates every tab's dashboards, a count says how much is left, and the active filter is legible from any tab.

anchors.1: Filters live per tab, or a tab ignores the panel.
anchors.3: Every tab follows the panel, but the count or the active filter is hard to see from a tab, or some figure does not recount.
anchors.5: Every figure on every tab recounts from the panel, says it is a subset (n of N), and the filter is visible on every tab.

requirements.name: Organised around the target trajectory, Dataset → Target → Run
requirements.why: Nov 19: "the Target trajectory is kinda the primary thing we want to organize things around"; levels dataset → targets (table or cards) → runs sortable by date, config, sim/real; Nov 24: "for the single target trajectory now your atomic unit is actually runs ... we are repeating the exact same pattern again and again".
requirements.passCondition: From the landing, one target's runs (grouped/sortable by config, sim/real) are two clicks away; the current level is always visible; the way back is one click.

anchors.1: Targets are only rows in a table; runs of one target cannot be compared in the frame.
anchors.3: The target level exists but leaves the frame (a different page/layout), or the level is hard to tell.
anchors.5: The same frame serves Dataset and Target, the level is always shown, and a target's runs sit in the panel with colour + checkbox, sortable by config / kind.

requirements.name: Which config is best, at a glance
requirements.why: Nov 20: "At the highest level we want to be comparing different pipeline configurations vs how they do on all of the targets"; Nov 23 picked the league table.
requirements.passCondition: The landing tab shows the config ranking, its magnitude (ratio to best) and n above the fold at 1440 x 900.

anchors.1: The ranking needs scrolling or reading many charts.
anchors.3: Visible, but needs several numbers or a second tab.
anchors.5: League above the fold: rank, value, ratio, n, sparkline per KPI, recounted by the panel.

requirements.name: Compact and embeddable
requirements.why: Nov 24 on the coverage round: "Its basically the tensor flow layout but I don't like the tabs here at the top top as then its harder to put it in another app"; "I want the viewer to be a bit more compact ... so it can drop into anything".
requirements.passCondition: The tabs belong to the component (not the browser page's top bar), the panel folds, no tab is taller than ~3 screens at 1440 x 900, and the layout still works at a ~1000 px wide box.

anchors.1: Page-level chrome; long scroll per tab; breaks narrow.
anchors.3: Compact tabs but page-level header, or one tab runs long.
anchors.5: Component-scoped tabs, foldable panel, every tab within ~2 screens, usable at 1000 px.

requirements.name: Selection and colour mean the same thing on every tab
requirements.why: TensorBoard / W&B convention: a run's colour and visibility are global; Nov 19: "I like the control over how the lines are showing".
requirements.passCondition: Hiding a config, recolouring or pinning in the panel changes every tab the same way; a config is the same colour everywhere.

anchors.1: Each tab has its own legend and visibility.
anchors.3: Colours are global but visibility or pins are per tab.
anchors.5: One selection model: colour, visibility and pins propagate to every tab and survive a reload.

requirements.name: Built from stock parts; short path to production
requirements.why: about-me: "Off-the-shelf first, not productization"; Nov 24: "we don't need to reinvent the wheel here"; data-ui landed <data-scope>/<data-workbench> (CONTRACT §53) for exactly this pattern the same day; traj_compare's Part E already has the tabs + league.
requirements.passCondition: The variant reuses a stock pattern (TensorBoard conventions, data-ui scope/workbench, traj_compare's existing levels and league) and its production path is named and short.

anchors.1: A new bespoke shell with no stock counterpart.
anchors.3: Bespoke shell following stock conventions, or stock parts with large gaps to fill.
anchors.5: Stock parts end to end (or the existing traj_compare levels extended), gaps named and small.

gates.name: Real bench data
gates.condition: Opens the UR5e site and at least one of BAM FB / pendulum from the bench's own traj_compare payloads; no invented numbers.

gates.name: file://, no network
gates.condition: Opens from file:// with no CDN, no build step, no server.

gates.name: The pattern
gates.condition: A left filter panel, tabs on top, dashboards per tab; the panel's edge drags (width remembered) and the panel folds.

gates.name: League + Coverage kept
gates.condition: The League table is the Overview (or landing) and Coverage is reachable (link or tab).

gates.name: Clean
gates.condition: No console or page errors and no sideways scroll at 1440 x 900 on any tab.
